p0.original: 关键问题：什么是心理学，什么不是心理学
p0.en: Question: What's psychology? What's not psychology?

p2.original: 心理学是一个广阔的领域，包括许多专业方向，但从根本上说，心理学是一门研究行为和心理过程的科学。
p2.en: Psychology is a broad field, encompassing many professional directions, but fundamentally it is a science of behaviour and psychological processes.

p3.original: “请你不要对我进行精神分析。”办公室门口的一个学生说道。这是心理学教授经常要面对的抗拒和职业性风险。但是，学生并不需要担心被精神分析，原因有二。其一，并不是所有的心理学家都能诊断和处理心理问题，事实上，在心理学教授中能这样做的只占少数；其二，只有少数心理学家是精神分析学家。精神分析（psychoanalysis）一词指的是一种高度专业化且相对少见的治疗形式。在第一章后面的内容中，你会进一步了解心理学家和精神分析学家之间的区别，但与此同时，不用担心你的教授会试图发现你有什么不对的地方。事实上，你的教授对如何帮助你学习更感兴趣，而不是寻找心理障碍的征兆。
p3.en: “Please don't give me a psychoanalytical analysis. A student at the office door said, This is the resistance and occupational risk that psychologists often face. However, students do not need to fear psychoanalysis for two reasons. First, not all psychologists are able to diagnose and deal with psychological problems, and in fact only a few of them are able to do so; Second, only a few psychologists are psychoanalysts. The term "psychoanalysis " refers to a highly specialized and relatively rare form of treatment. At the end of chapter I, you will learn more about the distinction between psychologists and psychoanalysts, but at the same time, don't worry about what your professor will try to find out about you. In fact, your professor is more interested in how to help you learn than in finding signs of psychological handicaps.

p4.original: 所以，你可能会想，如果心理学不仅仅是关于精神障碍和治疗的，那么它究竟是关于什么的呢？
p4.en: So you might wonder, if psychology is not just about psychosis and therapy, what is it about?

p5.original: 心理学（psychology）一词来源于古希腊语“psyche”，意为“心灵”，其后缀“ology”的意思是“一个研究领域”。所以，从字面上看，心理学即为“对心灵的研究”。然而，大多数心理学家采用的是本节核心概念中给出的这个更为宽泛的定义：
p5.en: The term "psychology" is derived from the ancient Greek word "psyche" meaning "the mind", followed by the word "logy" meaning "a field of study". So, literally speaking, psychology is “research on the mind”. However, most psychologists have adopted this broader definition, which is given in the core concept of this section:

p6.original: 心理学是一个广阔的领域，包括许多专业方向，但从根本上说，心理学是一门研究行为和心理过程的科学。
p6.en: Psychology is a broad field, encompassing many professional directions, but fundamentally it is a science of behaviour and psychological processes.

p7.original: 对于这个定义，我们需要注意的第一个重点是：心理学不仅包括心理过程，也包括行为。换言之，心理学领域涵盖了我们无法直接观察到的内部心理过程（如思考、感觉和愿望），以及能够直接观察到的外在行为（如说话、微笑和跑步）。定义中的第二个重点与心理学的科学要素有关。简而言之，心理学的科学性建立在客观、可验证的证据之上，不像在非科学领域中，仅有专家和权威人士的意见。我们会在本章结尾处为心理科学给出更完整的释义。而现在，让我们更近距离地了解一下心理学家实际的工作内容吧。
p7.en: The first focus of our attention to this definition is that psychology includes not only psychological processes but also behaviours. In other words, the area of psychology covers internal psychological processes (e.g. thinking, feeling and desire) that we cannot observe directly, as well as outward behaviour (e.g. speaking, smiling and running). The second focus of the definition relates to the scientific elements of psychology. In short, the scientific nature of psychology is based on objective and verifiable evidence, unlike in the non-scientific field, where the opinions of experts and authorities are limited. At the end of this chapter, we will give a more complete interpretation of the psychological sciences. Now, let's get a closer look at the actual work of psychologists.

p9.en: 1.1 Description of the different professional orientations that make up psychology.

p10.original: 1.2 区分心理学与伪心理学。

p13.original: 描述构成心理学的不同专业方向。
p13.en: Describe the different professional directions that make up psychology.

p14.original: 心理学涵盖的领域比大多数人认为的更广泛。正如前文所述，并不是所有的心理学家都是治疗师。许多心理学家从事教育、工业、体育工作，就职于监狱、政府、教堂、寺庙、私人诊所以及高校和社区学院的心理学系等。
p14.en: Psychology covers a wider range of areas than most people think. As noted earlier, not all psychologists are therapists. Many psychologists work in education, industry and sports, working in prisons, government, churches, temples, private clinics, as well as in the psychology departments of higher education and community colleges.

p15.original: 也有心理学家在工程公司、咨询公司以及法院工作（包括司法机构和NBA机构）（见图1-1）。
p15.en: Psychologists also work in engineering companies, consulting firms and courts (including the judiciary and NBA institutions) (see figures 1-1).

p16.original: 在各种各样的环境中，心理学家从事着各式各样的工作，包括教学、研究、测试、设备设计以及心理治疗。实际上，心理学的专业方向多到无法枚举，但我们可以先把心理学分为三大类，带你从中领略这一领域的多样性。
p16.en: In a variety of settings, psychologists perform a wide variety of tasks, including teaching, research, testing, equipment design and psychotherapy. In fact, psychology is so specialized that it cannot be counted, but first we can divide psychology into three broad categories, from which we can draw the diversity in this field.

p18.en: Note: Psychologists work in a wide variety of fields and in a variety of places.

p19.original: 1.1.1 从事心理学工作的三条途径
p19.en: 1.1.1 Three ways of working in psychology

p20.original: 广而言之，心理学家可以分为三个主要类别：
p20.en: More broadly, psychologists can be divided into three main categories:

p24.original: 不过，这三个群体存在一些重叠，因为很多心理学家在他们的工作中扮演着多重角色。
p24.en: However, there is some overlap between these three groups, as many psychologists play multiple roles in their work.

p25.original: 实验心理学家（有时被称为研究型心理学家）是三个群体中规模最小的。然而，是他们开展了大部分科研工作，创造了新的心理学知识（Frincke & Pate，2004）[1]。比如，一位实验心理学家完全有能力研究糖对儿童亢奋的影响。虽然在一些工业领域或私营研究机构也能看到一些实验心理学家的身影，但大多数实验心理学家在高校或社区学院开展科学研究并从事教学工作。
p25.en: Experimental psychologists (sometimes referred to as research psychologists) are the smallest of the three groups. However, it was they who carried out most of the scientific work and created new psychological knowledge (Frincke & Pate, 2004) [1]. For example, an experimental psychologist is fully capable of studying the effects of sugar on children's high levels of intensity. Although some experimental psychologists are also visible in some industrial fields or private research institutions, most of them conduct scientific research and teach at higher educational institutions or community colleges.

p26.original: 心理学教师通常在高校、2年制或4年制社区学院以及高中里工作。传统上，高校和社区学院的教师也肩负着做研究、发表论文、出版专著的工作，因此他们在同时扮演着心理学教师和实验心理学家的双重角色。在社区学院，心理学教师更专注于教学，当然也有人在教学的同时为科研做出了少许贡献（通常是次要追求）。高中教师很少有科研的任务（American Psychological Association，2007；Johnson & Rudmann，2004）。
p26.en: Psychologists usually work in higher schools, two-year or four-year community colleges and high schools. Traditionally, teachers in higher education and community colleges have also been assigned the task of researching, publishing papers and publishing monographs, so that they have a dual role as psychologists and experimental psychologists. In community colleges, psychology teachers are more focused on teaching, although there are also some who have contributed to scientific research at the same time (usually secondary pursuit). There are few scientific tasks for high school teachers (American Psychological Association, 2007); Johnson & Rudmann, 2004.

p27.original: 应用心理学家运用实验心理学家研究所得的知识来解决人们遇到的各种问题，如玩具或设备设计、犯罪分析和心理治疗。他们的工作场所多种多样，从学校、诊所、社会服务机构到工厂、机场、医院和赌场。总的看来，美国大约有三分之二的博士水平的心理学家从事应用心理学领域的工作（Wicherski et al.，2009）。
p27.en: Using the knowledge acquired by the Institute of Experimental Psychologists, psychologists are used to solve problems encountered, such as toy or equipment design, crime analysis and psychological treatment. Their workplaces range from schools, clinics, social services to factories, airports, hospitals and casinos. Overall, approximately two thirds of PhD-level psychologists in the United States work in the field of applied psychology (Wicherski et al., 2009).

p29.original: 一些最受欢迎的应用心理学专业如下。
p29.en: Some of the most popular applied psychology professions are described below.

p30.original: 工业组织心理学家（通常称为I/O心理学家）专门从事人员筛选、人才管理以及改善工作环境的工作，以将生产力和雇员士气最大化。作为心理学中发展最快的领域之一，工业组织心理学家就业的大大小小的公司遍布世界各地。例如，他们可以设计一些项目来激励员工或者提高管理者的领导能力。工业组织心理学家的工作也包括市场调研，给员工和管理层提供指导，调查员工满意度，以及帮助员工更好地平衡工作和个人生活（Novotney，2011；Shrader，2001）。
p30.en: Industrial organization psychologists (commonly known as I/O psychologists) specialize in the screening of personnel, talent management and improvement of the working environment in order to maximize productivity and employee morale. As one of the fastest-growing areas of psychology, the companies in which psychologists from industrial organizations are employed are located around the world. For example, they could design projects to motivate staff or enhance managerial leadership. The work of industry organization psychologists also includes market research, guidance to staff and management, surveys of employee satisfaction and assistance to staff to better balance work and personal life (Novotney, 2011); Shrader, 2001.

p31.original: 运动心理学家通过规划有效的训练方案，提高运动员的积极性，以及指导运动员如何在压力下控制情绪，从而改善他们的表现。有些运动心理学家只为职业运动员提供服务，有些则与体育爱好者共事。还有一些从业者与以体力活动为主要工作内容的个体一起工作，比如，消防员或某些军事人员。在所有这些情况下，心理学家的目标是帮助他们的客户通过克服任何可能存在的心理障碍，最大限度地提高他们的表现。运动心理学家也可以开展研究，以更好地理解心理和表现之间的关系，例如，研究各种人格类型为何有可能会增加对高风险运动（如救火、跳伞或潜水）的兴趣。
p31.en: Sports psychologists improve their performance by planning effective training programmes, increasing the motivation of athletes and providing guidance to athletes on how to control their emotions under stress. Some sports psychologists serve only professional athletes, while others work with sports fans. There are also practitioners working with individuals whose work is dominated by physical activity, such as firefighters or certain military personnel. In all these cases, the aim of the psychologist is to help their clients to maximize their performance by overcoming any psychological barriers that may exist. Sports psychologists can also undertake research to better understand the relationship between psychology and performance, for example, to examine why various personality types may increase interest in high-risk movements (e.g., fire relief, jump or dive).

p32.original: 学校心理学家是教学与学习领域的专家。他们处理影响学业、家庭的问题，或是影响在校表现的个人危机问题，或是如拉帮结派、青少年怀孕或药物滥用等社会问题。有时他们还会对学习或行为问题做出诊断，与教师、学生和家长合作，帮助学生顺利完成学业。许多学校心理学家为学区工作，他们的工作包括实施心理测验、评分并且解读测验结果。
p32.en: School psychologists are specialists in the field of teaching and learning. They deal with issues that affect schooling, families, or personal crises that affect school performance, or social problems such as gangs, teenage pregnancy or substance abuse. Sometimes they also diagnose learning or behavioural problems and work with teachers, students and parents to help students complete their studies successfully. Many school psychologists work for the school district, and their work includes conducting psychological tests, scoring and interpreting the results.

p33.original: 临床与咨询心理学家帮助人们在人际关系、职业或教育上做出艰难的选择，帮他们更好地适应社会、调整情绪。约有半数的博士水平的心理学家将临床与咨询作为他们的职业（Wicherski et al.，2009）。
p33.en: Clinical and counselling psychologists help people make difficult choices about relationships, careers or education, and help them better adapt to society and to their emotions. About half of the doctoral psychologists consider clinical and counselling as their profession (Wicherski et al., 2009).

p34.original: 司法心理学家为法律和司法系统提供心理学专业知识。作为近年被认可的心理学专业之一，法律心理学的迅速走红一定程度上归功于《犯罪心理》（Criminal Minds）、《犯罪现场调查》（CSI）这类电视剧的播出。尽管现实中的司法心理学家不像电视里的同行那样耀眼夺目或行事爽利，但这个领域的发展生机勃勃，充满了各种各样的机会。司法心理学家会对监狱里的犯人或司法医院中的病人实施测验，以确认这些人是否可以被释放或者是否可以接受审判；他们还会在强奸或虐童案件中评估证词，或者帮助法院挑选陪审团成员（Clay，2009b；Huss，2001）。
p34.en: Judicial psychologists provide psychological expertise to the legal and judicial system. As one of the recognized psychology professions of recent years, the rapid expansion of legal psychology is partly attributable to the broadcasting of television shows such as Crime Minds, Crime Scene Investigation (CSI). Although judicial psychologists in reality are not as bright or as good as their counterparts on television, the development of this field is dynamic and full of opportunities. (b) Judicial psychologists test prisoners in prisons or patients in judicial hospitals to determine whether they can be released or tried; They also assess testimony in cases of rape or child abuse or help the court to select jury members (Clay, 2009b); Huss, 2001.

p35.original: 环境心理学家的目标是改善人类与环境的关系。比如，他们会研究城市内的园林对儿童学习成绩的影响，或者确定鼓励环保行为的方法，如回收再利用。环境心理学家有时会帮助客户遵守他们对可持续性发展的承诺，或者开办工作坊来告诉人们与自然互动对心理健康的益处（Novotney，2009）。
p35.en: The goal of environmental psychologists is to improve the relationship between human beings and the environment. For example, they will study the impact of gardens in cities on children's learning performance or identify ways to encourage environmentally friendly behaviour, such as recycling. Environmental psychologists sometimes help clients to comply with their commitment to sustainable development, or run workshops to inform people about the benefits of interacting with nature on mental health (Novotney, 2009).

p36.original: 老年心理学家是心理学大家庭中的最新成员之一。随着美国65岁以上老年人口的快速增长，美国心理学会建立了专业老年心理学，帮助老年人保持健康喜乐，以及有效应对与年龄相关的挑战。老年心理学家实施评估，提供干预，并与家人、护理人员和医疗专业人员协商，来帮助老年人在他们生命的后期最大限度地发挥潜力。
p36.en: Senior psychologists are one of the newest members of the family of psychology. With the rapid growth of older people over 65 years of age in the United States, the American Psychological Association has established professional geriatrics to help older people remain healthy and happy, as well as to respond effectively to age-related challenges. Senior psychologists carry out assessments, provide interventions and consult with families, caregivers and medical professionals to help older persons maximize their potential in the later stages of their lives.

p37.original: 想要了解更多有关心理学职业的信息，读者可以查阅美国心理学会出版的《心理学职业》（Careers in Psychology）（2011a）等出版物。
p37.en: Readers can consult publications such as Careers in Psycology (2011a) published by the American Psychological Association to obtain more information about the psychology profession.

p39.original: 如同心理学的初学者会认为心理学家都是临床心理学家一样，可能他们也不清楚心理学与精神病学的区别。你或许也会在测试时遇到这道题，就让我们来消除这种混淆吧。
p39.en: As in the case of prima facie psychologists, who consider them to be clinical psychologists, perhaps they are not aware of the difference between psychology and psychiatry. You may also have this problem at the test, so let's get rid of this confusion.

p40.original: 几乎所有的精神科医生都治疗心理障碍，但只有一部分心理学家可以治疗精神障碍，它们之间的相似点也仅限于此。精神病学（psychiatry）属于医学专业，而不是心理学的一部分。精神科医生取得的是医学博士学位，接受过心理及行为问题治疗特别是药物治疗的专门训练。因此，精神科医生有行医和处方权，他们倾向于治疗患有较严重精神障碍的病人（如精神分裂症），并会从医学的角度来看待病人，把他们看作患有精神“疾病”的人。
p40.en: Almost all psychiatrists treat mental disorders, but only some psychologists can treat mental disorders, and the similarities between them are limited. Psychiatry is a medical profession and not a part of psychology. The psychiatrist has obtained a doctorate in medicine and has received specialized training in psycho-behavioural and behavioural treatments, especially medication. As a result, psychiatrists have the right to practice medicine and prescription, preferring to treat patients with more severe mental disorders (e.g. schizophrenia) and to view patients from a medical point of view as having mental “diseases”.

p41.original: 与精神病学相比，心理学涵盖的范围更广，它包括人类的所有行为与心理过程，从大脑功能到社会互动，从心理健康到精神障碍。大多数心理学家在研究生期间的训练重点是研究方法，以及对心理学特定领域的深入研究。另外，虽然心理学家通常都拥有博士学位，但他们接受的并非医学训练，因此他们一般没有处方权。但是近年来，美国的一些州通过了立法，允许合格的心理学家开某些处方药，但必须完成一些高级培训和认证（APA，2014）。总之，心理学家从事的领域非常广泛，并且都是从心理学的角度来看待人。临床与咨询心理学家会把人们看作需要帮助的来访者，而非病人。
p41.en: The scope of psychology is broader than that of psychiatry, which encompasses all human behaviour and psychological processes, from brain function to social interaction, from mental health to mental disorders. Most of the training of psychologists during postgraduate studies focuses on research methods and on in-depth research in specific areas of psychology. Moreover, although psychologists usually hold doctoral degrees, they do not receive medical training, and therefore they generally have no prescription power. In recent years, however, some states in the United States have passed legislation allowing qualified psychologists to prescribe certain prescription drugs, but some advanced training and certification has to be completed (APA, 2014). In general, psychologists are involved in a wide range of fields and are viewed from a psychological perspective. Clinical and consulting psychologists see people as visitors in need of help, not as patients.

p42.original: 现在你知道精神病学不是心理学了。接下来，我们将探讨另一个经常与心理学混淆的领域：伪心理学（pseudo-psychology）。
p42.en: Now you know psychiatry is not psychology. Next, we will explore another area that is often confused with psychology: pseudo-psychologic.

p43.original: 1.2 对心理学与伪心理学的批判性思考
p43.en: 1.2 Critical reflections on psychology and pseudopsychology

p45.original: 区分心理学与伪心理学。

p46.original: 像《露西》（Lucy）和《X战警》（X-Men）这样的热门电影延续了一个悠久的娱乐传统，它们使观众着迷于精神层面的神秘力量及其影响人类行为的超自然作用。
p46.en: Hot films such as Lucy and X-Men continue a long tradition of entertainment, which ensnares audiences with the mysterious forces of spirituality and their supernatural effects on human behaviour.

p47.original: 你每天查看的星座运程，以及已被彻底揭穿是骗局的占星术均在此列（Schick & Vaughn，2001）。笔迹学（一种进行笔迹分析的伪科学）、算命或者能让人花钱购物的潜意识信息这些也没有任何事实依据。所有这些都属于伪心理学的范畴：伪装成科学真理但实际都是毫无依据的心理学信念。
p47.en: The constellations you see every day are listed here, as well as as the asterisks that have been thoroughly uncovered (Schick & Vaughn, 2001). Nor is there any factual basis for handwriting (a pseudo-scientific science of handwriting analysis), fortune tellers or sublime information that can make people buy. All of this falls within the realm of pseudo-psychology: disguised as scientific truth, but in fact unfounded psychological conviction.

p48.original: 由帕特里克·斯图尔特（Patrick Stewart）扮演的《X战警》中的X教授拥有超能力，这想象起来可能很有趣——但没有科学依据。
p48.en: Professor X of the X-Police, played by Patrick Stewart, had superpowers, which could be interesting -- no scientific basis.

p49.original: 当然，要是将星座和特异功能的题材视为纯粹的娱乐，那确实很有趣，但我们必须认识到，一旦真相不复存在，幻想就会滋生。毕竟，你不会想将涉及健康或福利的重要决定建立在虚假的信息上，不是吗？因此，本书的目标之一就是帮助你批判性地思考那些关于行为与心理过程的不寻常的说法。而且，为了避免你误认为“批判性思维”只是让你设法批评，让我们澄清一下这个重要术语在本书中的真实含义。
p49.en: Of course, it would be interesting to see the subject of constellations and features as purely entertainment, but we have to realize that once the truth has disappeared, illusions breed. After all, you don't want to base important decisions about health or well-being on false information, do you? So one of the aims of this book is to help you critically think about the unusual things about behavior and psychological processes. Moreover, in order to avoid your mistaken view that “critical thinking” is merely a way for you to try to criticize, let us clarify the true meaning of this important term in this book.

p51.original: 那些谈论批判性思维（critical thinking）的人经常发现自己像是美国最高法院的大法官波特·斯图尔特（Potter Stewart），他有一句名言，“我不能给色情下定义，但我一看就知道它是不是。”就像斯图尔特法官一样，本书的作者们也无法提出一个无可争议的对批判性思维的定义。不过，我们愿意转而探讨将在本书中强调的6种批判性思维技能（critical thinking skills）。每一种技能都基于一个我们认为在面对新想法时应该提出的具体问题。
p51.en: Those who talk about critical thinking often find themselves like Potter Stewart, the Supreme Court of the United States, who famously says, "I can't define pornography, but I know it isn't. “Like Judge Stewart, the authors of this book are not in a position to propose an undisputed definition of critical thinking. However, we would like to turn to the six critical thinking skills that will be highlighted in this book. Each skill is based on a specific issue that we believe should be raised in the face of new ideas.

p52.en: 1. Where are the sources of the view?

p53.original: 2. 观点是合理的还是极端的？
p53.en: 2. Is the view reasonable or extreme?

p55.original: 4. 相关结论是否存在被偏差污染的可能？
p55.en: 4. Are there risks of contamination by deviations?

p56.original: 5. 推理过程是否避免了常见谬误？
p56.en: 5. Has the reasoning process avoided common errors?

p57.en: 6. Is there a need for a pluralistic perspective?

p58.original: 观点的来源是哪里 提出某个观点的人是否具有相关领域的实际专业知识？比如，假设你听到一则新闻，一名政客或权威人士宣称未成年的违法者被恐吓后会改过自新。新闻解释说，在该项目中，初犯者会受到如重罪犯一样近乎非人般的虐待，试图用可怕的监狱生活故事吓唬初犯者，使其远离犯罪。事实上，美国的很多州以及其他一些国家都曾经尝试过这种项目（Petrosino et al.，2013）。但是，主张这一观点的人确实具备这方面的知识吗？他们具有合法的资质吗？还是他们只是自称“专家”？找出答案的方法之一是上网检查这些人的证明文件及其在相关领域内的地位。而且，还要查出发表观点的人是否因此获得实质性利益。比如，如果这是一项医学突破，发表观点的人是否能从新药或医疗设备中获取利益？在“恐吓从善”的项目中，发表观点的人是否在试图搞政绩、拉选票，或者在为电视节目做宣传？
p58.en: Where does the point of view come from and does the person who put it forward have practical expertise in the relevant field? For example, if you hear a news story, a politician or an authoritative person claims that a minor offender is intimidated and will be rehabilitated. The press explained that, under the project, first-time offenders were subjected to almost inhuman abuse, as were serious criminals, in an attempt to scare the first-timers away from the crime with a terrible prison life story. In fact, many states in the United States, as well as some others, have tried such projects (Petrosino et al., 2013). But do those who advocate this view indeed have knowledge of it? Do they have legal qualifications? Or are they just calling themselves "experts"? One way to find out the answer is to check online the documentation of these persons and their position in the relevant field. Furthermore, it is necessary to find out whether the person who expressed his views received substantive benefits as a result. For example, if this is a medical breakthrough, can those who express their views benefit from new medicines or medical equipment? In the “Intimidation of Good Work” project, are those who express their views trying to make a difference, to pull votes, or to promote television programmes?

p59.original: “恐吓从善”项目可能会吸引绝望的父母，但研究表明这类项目并不有效——实际上，它们反而会提高青少年犯罪率。如果你将我们的6种批判性思维技能应用于这一观点以及其他流行的观点，将有助于你成为更明智的信息消费者。
p59.en: “Intimidation and charity” projects may attract desperate parents, but studies have shown that such projects are not effective — in fact, they increase juvenile delinquency rates. If you apply our six critical thinking skills to this and other popular ideas, it will help you become a wiser consumer of information.

p60.original: 观点是合理的还是极端的 人生苦短，当然不能对一切都持批判性态度，所以关键是要有所选择。怎么选择？正如著名天文学家卡尔·萨根（Carl Sagan）在谈到外星人绑架的报告时曾说：“不寻常的观点需要不寻常的证据。”（Nova Online，1996）因此，批判性思考者会对那些被吹捧为“突破”或“革命”的说法持怀疑态度。当然，偶尔确实会有突破或革命性的新疗法奏效——但它们相对少见。大多数新的科学发展是在现有知识上的延伸。因此，那些与公认的知识有冲突的说法应当引起你的警惕。比如，你要提防那些宣称不需要付出太多努力就能帮人们戒烟或减肥的广告。对于“恐吓从善”或其他快速解决难题的方法，你要谨记：用简单方法就能解决复杂问题实属罕见。
p60.en: The point is whether it's reasonable or extreme, life is short, certainly not critical of everything, so the key is to make choices. How? As Carl Sagan, a famous astronomer, said in the report on the abduction of aliens: “Unusual views require unusual evidence. Thus, critical thinkers would be sceptical about what they termed a “break-through” or a “revolution”. Of course, sometimes breakthroughs or revolutionary new therapies do work — they are relatively rare. Most of the new scientific developments are an extension of existing knowledge. Therefore, those claims that conflict with recognized knowledge should draw your attention. For example, you need to guard against advertising that says that you don't have to do much to help people quit smoking or lose weight. With regard to “intimidation and good” or other quick solutions to difficult problems, remember that it is rare to solve complex problems in a simple way.

p61.original: 证据是什么 这是进行批判性思维的最重要的指导方针之一。你将在本章的其他地方了解到更多关于科学证据是由什么构成的知识。不过，现在，我们要提防轶事证据（anecdotal evidence）或声称新计划有惊人效果的证词。这些第一手的叙述听起来很有说服力，常常诱使我们相信它们。然而，这种轶事和证词无论听起来多有说服力，它们都不是科学证据。它们仅代表了少数被精心挑选出的个体经历。将适合少数人的事物推断为一定适合所有人，这是有风险的，甚至是危险的。
p61.en: What evidence is is one of the most important guidelines for critical thinking. You will learn more about what constitutes scientific evidence elsewhere in this chapter. However, we are now trying to guard against anecdotal evidence or testimony alleging that the new plan has had an alarming effect. These first-hand accounts sound persuasive and often induce us to believe them. However, no matter how persuasive such indecency and testimony may sound, they are not scientific evidence. They represent only a few carefully selected individual experiences. It is risky, if not dangerous, to infer that what is appropriate for a few is necessarily for all.

p62.original: “恐吓从善”项目的证据是什么？毫无疑问，它们不起作用。事实上，大量科学证据表明，平均而言，接受“恐吓从善”疗法的青少年比没有接受的青少年随后陷入更多的麻烦（Petrosino et al.，2012）。不仅如此，美国司法部还强烈指责这些项目，批评它们造成的伤害（Robinson & Slowikowski，2011）。
p62.en: What is the evidence of the “Intimidation of Good Will” project? There is no doubt that they do not work. In fact, there is a wealth of scientific evidence that on average adolescents who receive “terror” therapy are in more trouble than those who do not (Petrosino et al., 2012). In addition, the United States Department of Justice has strongly accused these projects of harm caused (Robinson & Slowikowski, 2011).

p63.original: 相关结论是否存在会被偏差污染的可能 批判性思考者知道在什么情况下有可能出现偏差，并且可以辨认出常见的偏差类型，其中的大部分我们会在本书中探讨。但是现在，让我们先看其中一些偏差类型。
p63.en: And if there's a possibility of being contaminated with bias, then critical thinkers know the circumstances under which deviations may occur and can identify common types of deviations, most of which we will look at in this book. But now, let's look at some of these types of deviations.

p64.original: 与“恐吓从善”案例最为契合的偏差形式是情感偏差（emotional bias）：许多忧心忡忡的父母不停地联系执法部门，要求他们的孩子参加这类项目，称他们束手无策，不知道还能向谁求助。他们不顾一切地寻求帮助，依赖大众媒体和他们在电视上看到的东西，并将其作为指导，而不是清醒地思考，寻找有成功证据的替代项目（Yu，2014）。此外，人们对犯罪行为和罪犯的恐惧可能会促使人们支持对犯罪行为实施严惩，颁布的一连串“三振出局”法律（规定在三次重罪定罪后判处终身监禁）就是证明。
p64.en: The most relevant form of bias in the case of “terror and charity” is emotional bias: many worried parents keep in contact with the law enforcement authorities and ask their children to participate in such projects, claiming that they are helpless and do not know who else to turn to. They are desperate to seek help, relying on the mass media and what they see on television, and using it as a guide rather than a sobering thought and finding alternative projects with evidence of success (Yu, 2014). Furthermore, fear of criminal acts and offenders may encourage support for the imposition of severe penalties for criminal acts, as evidenced by the enactment of a series of “triple strikes” laws, which provide for life imprisonment after three convictions for serious crimes.

p65.original: 证实性偏差（confirmation bias）是另一种常见的偏差类型，即人类倾向于记住证实自己信念的事件，忽略或忘记矛盾的证据（Halpern，2002；Nickerson，1998）。比如，证实性偏差解释了为什么人们坚持相信占星术有效：他们只记住了看起来准确的预测，忘掉了那些错误的预测。证实性偏差也解释了为什么赌徒更容易回忆起自己赢钱的那一刻，而不是输钱的情景，或者为什么我们坚持认为某个物品是我们的幸运物。令人惊讶的是，最近的研究表明，这种偏见可能部分是生物学性质的。在一项于总统大选前完成的研究中，人们听到他们最喜欢的政客发表的自相矛盾的言论时，其大脑中与推理有关的回路会突然关闭，而与情绪相关的脑区仍然活跃（Shermer，2006；Westen et al.，2006）。此刻大脑在说，“我不想听到任何与我的信念冲突的东西。”因此，为了避免这种偏差，我们可能不得不付出额外的努力。
p65.en: Proof of sexual bias (conversion bias) is another common type of bias in which human beings tend to remember events that confirm their beliefs and ignore or forget contradictory evidence (Halapern, 2002); Nickerson, 1998. For example, the validation deviation explains why people insist on believing that astrologer works: they only remember what seems to be accurate predictions, and forget what is wrong with them. Proofing deviations also explain why gamblers are easier to remember when they win, not when they lose, or why we insist that something is our lucky thing. Surprisingly, recent studies have shown that such prejudices may be partly biological in nature. In a study completed prior to the presidential election, when people heard contradictory statements from their favorite politicians, the reasoning-related circuits in their brain were suddenly closed, while the emotional-related brain zone remained active (Shermer, 2006); Westen et al., 2006). And the brain is saying, "I don't want to hear anything that conflicts with my beliefs. We may therefore have to make extra efforts to avoid such a deviation.

p66.original: 推理过程是否避免了常见谬误 在本书中我们会探讨几种常见谬误，例如“恐吓从善”这一观点的谬误就是用常识替代科学证据。事实上，在很多情况下，一个问题的两个方面都拥有支持它们的常识。比如，我们都知道“物以类聚，人以群分”，但也知道“异性相吸”的说法。同样，我们常被提醒“早起的鸟儿有虫吃”，但不也常被告诫“欲速则不达”吗？那么，哪种说法才是正确的呢？只有对证据进行检验才能得到可信的答案。
p66.en: Whether or not the reasoning has avoided common errors, we will explore in this book a few common errors, such as the fallacy of the notion of “intimidation for good”, which is to substitute common sense for scientific evidence. In fact, in many cases, both sides of a problem have common sense of support for them. We all know, for example, that things are clustered in groups, but we also know the term “smoothing of the opposite sex”. Similarly, we are often reminded that “early-rised birds eat insects”, but are not often warned that “fast-to-fast” is not enough? So, which is the correct one? Only a test of the evidence can provide a credible answer.

p67.original: 再举一个关于逻辑谬误的例子——当两个事物存在关联时，其中一方的发生一定会导致另一方的发生。这被称为相关-因果谬误（correlation-causation fallacy）。例如，你知道当人们吃掉更多的冰淇淋时，谋杀率会上升吗？这是真实的——有明确的数据支持它们之间的关联。然而，吃冰淇淋会导致人们互相残杀的假设听上去就很愚蠢。（想知道什么才是这一相关性的真正成因吗？你可以想想可能同时影响冰淇淋消费和攻击性的因素。）然而，当人类被要求解释事物时，我们通常会得出错误的结论，比如，随着越来越多的儿童接种疫苗，孤独症发病率也上升了。事实上，我们必须思考对这种关联的其他解释，并且要寻找额外的证据。
p67.en: A further example of a logical error — when two things are connected, the occurrence of one of them necessarily leads to the other. This is called the associated-causal error. For example, do you know that when people eat more ice cream, the murder rate increases? This is true — there are clear data to support their connection. However, the assumption that ice cream can cause people to kill each other sounds stupid. (Do you want to know what is the real cause of this correlation? You can think of factors that may influence ice cream consumption and aggression at the same time. However, when human beings are asked to explain things, we often arrive at the wrong conclusion, for example, that the incidence of autism has increased as more and more children are vaccinated. In fact, we must reflect on other interpretations of this connection and look for additional evidence.

p68.original: 是否需要多元化视角 大部分关乎人类的行为问题和社会问题都是复杂的，需要从多个角度看待才能完全理解。因此，批判性思考者知道不应接受只关注一个角度的观点。比如，“恐吓从善”的观点简单地假定对惩罚的恐惧就是对犯罪的最好威慑。一个更完备的观点会意识到还有其他因素导致了犯罪。比如，心理学家可能会将犯罪视为习得行为、社会影响或人格特质的产物；经济学家会对犯罪行为的经济诱因感兴趣；社会学家则会关注帮派、贫穷和社区结构等问题。当然，这样一个多元化的问题需要一个比惩罚威胁更复杂的解决办法。
p68.en: The need for a pluralistic perspective, which is complex in most of the issues of human behaviour and social issues, requires a number of perspectives to be fully understood. Therefore, critical thinkers know that one perspective should not be accepted. For example, from the perspective of “intimidation is good”, it is simply assumed that fear of punishment is the best deterrent to crime. A more complete view would recognize that there were other factors that led to crime. For example, psychologists may view crime as the product of acquired behaviour, social influence or personality characteristics; Economists will be interested in the economic incentives for criminal behaviour; Sociologists, for their part, focus on gangs, poverty and community structures. Of course, such a multifaceted problem requires a more complex solution than the threat of punishment.

p69.original: 对本章问题的批判性思考
p69.en: Critical reflections on the issue of this chapter

p70.original: 在向下推进之前，问问你自己：

p71.original: 对于开篇的“糖是否会让孩子亢奋”的问题，你会如何进行这些批判性思考？
p71.en: How do you think this is critical when you start with the question, "Will sugar make the child stride?"

p73.original: 这个8岁小孩的母亲是研究糖的生物学影响的专家吗？假设她不是，那么你必须思考她的观点来源是否可信，或她是否只是在复述她经常听到的“常识”，并且从未质疑。
p73.en: Is the mother of this eight-year-old an expert in the biological effects of sugar? If she is not, then you have to think about whether her sources are credible or whether she is merely repeating what she often hears of “common sense” and never questioning it.

p75.original: 做过糖对儿童行为影响的科学实验吗？如果做过，实验结果反映了什么？
p75.en: Have you ever had any scientific experiments on the effects of sugar on children's behaviour? If so, what does the results reflect?

p77.original: 比如，证实性偏差会让我们倾向于记住孩子们在吃糖后变得亢奋的情景，忘记或忽视他们吃糖后没有受到影响的情景。此外，期望偏差（expectancy bias）会让我们预期孩子在吃糖后会变得亢奋，于是这就成了我们看到的情况。
p77.en: For example, a confirmation bias tends to remind us of the situation in which children get high after eating sugar, and forget or ignore the situation in which they are not affected by eating sugar. Moreover, the expectation that deviations will make us expect children to become exult when they eat sugar, which is what we see.

p78.original: 4. 提出这个观点的人是否避开了推理中的常见谬误
p78.en: 4. Whether the person who presented this view avoided the common fallacy of reasoning

p79.original: 在这个例子中，即使我们能证明摄入更多糖的孩子更亢奋，我们也无法确定糖是导致亢奋的原因，因为它们之间的关系是有相关性的（没有显示出因果关系）。或者，也有可能是本就亢奋的孩子吃了更多的糖来维持他们高运动量的需求。又或许，是聚会的兴奋引发了亢奋，但被归因到了糖上。认识到这些可能性有助于我们克服相关-因果谬误。
p79.en: In this example, even if we can prove that more sugar is ingested by children, we cannot be sure that sugar is the cause of edgy because their relationship is relevant (no causality is shown). Or maybe the high-strung kids ate more sugar to sustain their high-motion demand. And perhaps the excitement of the party caused the excitement, but it was attributed to sugar. The recognition of these possibilities helps us to overcome the associated-cause-effect errors.

p80.original: 5. 还有哪些视角应被考量
p80.en: 5. What other perspectives should be taken into account

p81.original: 最后，认识多元化视角的需求让我们承认，可能还有其他原因致使孩子们在聚会上变得亢奋。比如，家长可能允许孩子在聚会上有更活泼的行为举止，同时儿童聚会的一般特点和社会规范实际上也需要充满活力的游戏。
p81.en: Finally, the need to recognize a diversity perspective leads us to acknowledge that there may be other reasons for children to get high at meetings. For example, parents may allow children to have more lively behaviour at meetings, while the general characteristics and social norms of children's gatherings actually require dynamic play.

p82.original: 试一试 心理科学还是臆想
p82.en: Try it. The psychology or the imagination.

p83.original: 现在让我们对你的心理信念进行一次抽样检验。以下陈述有些是正确的，有些是错误的。如果你没能答对其中一些题目，哪怕全部题目，也不必担心：因为很多人会和你一样。重点在于，所谓的关于我们心理过程的常识可能经不起科学测试的检验。请判断下列陈述的正误。
p83.en: Now let's take a sample of your mental beliefs. The following statement is some correct and some incorrect. If you fail to answer some of the questions, even all of them, there is no need to worry: because many people will be like you. The point is that so-called common sense about our psychological processes may not stand the test of science. Please judge whether the following statements are correct or incorrect.

p84.original: 1. ___大多数人只用到了自身大脑的10%的说法纯属无稽之谈。
p84.en: 1. _ _ The assertion that most people use only 10 per cent of their own brain is simply nonsense.

p85.original: 2. ___当梦中的场景特别真实时，你的身体处于麻痹状态。
p85.en: 2. _ When the scene of the dream is particularly real, your body is in a state of paralysis.

p87.original: 4. ___红色只是大脑的一种感觉。大脑以外的世界没有红色。
p87.en: 4. _ Red is just a feeling of the brain. There's no red outside the brain.

p88.original: 5. ___双相障碍（躁狂-抑郁）是由无意识的冲突造成的。
p88.en: 5. _ bipolar disorder (matisfactory-depressive) is caused by unintentional conflict.

p89.original: 6. ___新生儿的大脑是一块白板，他们知道的任何事情都是由经历“写”（经由学习）上去的。
p89.en: The brain of the newborn child is a white sheet, and everything they know is written through experience.

p90.original: 7. ___发生在我们身上的所有事情会永远保存在我们的记忆中。
p90.en: 7. _ Everything that happens to us will remain in our memory forever.

p91.original: 8. ___出生时你便拥有了一生中几乎全部的脑细胞。
p91.en: 8. _ At birth, you have almost all the brain cells of your life.

p92.original: 9. ___智力几乎完全取决于遗传，在人的一生中基本保持稳定不变。
p92.en: 9. _ Intellectuals depend almost entirely on genetics and remain largely stable throughout a person's life.

p93.original: 10. ___测谎仪可以准确探测人的身体反应，受过训练的检测者可以据此判断被测者何时在说谎。
p93.en: 10. A polygraph can accurately detect a person's physical reaction, and a trained detector can judge on that basis when the person being tested is lying.

p94.original: 前4条是正确的，其余都是错误的。
p94.en: The first four were correct, and the rest were wrong.

p95.original: 以下是对每一条的简要解释。
p95.en: The following is a brief explanation of each article.

p96.original: 随着你对心理学的学习进度的推进，你会了解到更多关于这些错误陈述的细节。
p96.en: As you advance in your study of psychology, you will learn more about these misrepresentations.

p97.original: 1. 正确：这纯属无稽之谈。我们每天都会用到大脑的所有脑区。
p97.en: Correct: This is simply nonsense. We use all the brain regions of the brain every day.

p98.original: 2. 正确：真实的梦境一般发生在快速眼动睡眠（REM）期间，人体除了控制眼睛的肌肉，其他随意肌都处于麻痹状态。
p98.en: 2. Correct: Real dreams usually occur during fast eye motion sleep (REM), when the body is paralysed with any muscle other than the muscles of the eye.

p99.original: 3. 正确：心理和身体的联系会使你在长期压力下患病。
p99.en: Correct: Psychological and physical contact can cause you to become ill under prolonged stress.

p100.original: 4. 正确：尽管这看似奇怪，但人的所有色彩感觉都是大脑本身产生的。光波确实具有不同的频率，却没有色彩。大脑把光的不同频率解读成不同的颜色。
p100.en: Correct: Although this may seem strange, all the colours of human beings are generated by the brain itself. The light waves do have different frequencies, but no color. The brain interprets the different frequencies of light into different colors.

p101.original: 5. 错误：没有证据能证明无意识的冲突会导致双相障碍。相反，证据表明双相障碍有很强的生物化学因素。某些药物对这一疾病很有效，这暗示了双相障碍涉及大脑中化学物质的缺陷。研究还表明，这种缺陷可能有遗传基础。
p101.en: Error: There is no evidence that an unconscious conflict can lead to double barriers. Instead, evidence suggests that the bipolar barrier has a strong biochemical factor. Certain drugs are effective for the disease, which suggests that dual-stage disorders involve chemical defects in the brain. The study also shows that this deficiency may have a genetic basis.

p102.original: 6. 错误：新生儿并非一块“白板”，而是有诸多先天能力和防御反射。“白板”谣言还忽略了儿童通过遗传而获得的潜力。
p102.en: Error: The newborn is not a “whiteboard”, but a number of congenital abilities and defensive reflections. The “whiteboard” rumour also ignores the genetic potential of children.

p103.original: 7. 错误：尽管我们能够记住很多生活细节，但没有证据证明我们能够记住人生中的所有细节。事实上，我们完全有理由相信，我们身边的大多数信息永远不会进入记忆，而那些进入记忆的信息也往往会变得失真。
p103.en: Error: While we can remember many details of life, there is no evidence that we can remember all the details of life. In fact, we have every reason to believe that most of the information around us will never go into memory, and that information that enters memory will often become distorted.

p104.original: 8. 错误：与科学家几年前所持的观点相悖，大脑的某些脑区在一生中都会持续产生新细胞。
p104.en: 8. Error: Contrary to what scientists held a few years ago, certain brain regions of the brain continue to produce new cells throughout their lifetime.

p105.original: 9. 错误：智力受遗传和环境的共同影响。由于智力的一部分受环境影响，人的智力水平（通过智商测验来衡量）在一生中是会发生变化的。
p105.en: Errors: Intellectuals are affected by the co-inheritance of genetics and the environment. Because part of the mental capacity is affected by environmental impacts, the intellectual level of a person (measured through an IQ test) changes over a lifetime.

p106.original: 10. 错误：最专业的测谎专家也有可能将说真话的人误判为说谎者，或者无法辨别出真正说谎的人。支持测谎仪准确性的客观证据很少。
p106.en: 10. Error: It is also possible that the most professional polygrapher misjudged the person who told the truth as a liar or could not identify the person who really lied. There is little objective evidence to support the accuracy of the polygraph.

p107.original: 心理学很有用 心理学专业

p108.original: 现在，你可能会想，心理学听起来很有趣。我应该考虑主修心理学吗？一个心理学的学位在很多方面都有用，不论你是否想成为心理学家。心理学的主要目标是更好地理解人类行为产生的原因，所以哪怕只上几堂心理学的课也会帮你更深入地理解生活中的自己和他人。获得心理学的学士学位可以为你胜任机构、医院、疗养院和康复中心的心理助理或技术员做准备。一个心理学学士学位，加上商业、政府、新闻或教育方面的职业训练，也足以作为进入这些职业领域的良好准备。
p108.en: Now, you might think, psychology sounds fun. Should I think about majoring in psychology? A degree in psychology is useful in many ways, whether you want to be a psychologist or not. The main objective of psychology is to better understand the causes of human behaviour, so even a few lessons in psychology will help you to understand yourself and others in life. A bachelor's degree in psychology can prepare for psychological assistants or technicians in competent institutions, hospitals, sanatoriums and rehabilitation centres. A bachelor's degree in psychology, combined with vocational training in commerce, government, journalism or education, is also sufficient to prepare well for entry into these professions.

p109.original: 然而，要成为一名成熟的心理学家，除了学士学位之外，还需要大量的培训。在研究生院，心理学系的学生需要修习一个或多个专业领域中的高级课程，同时需要发展学者和研究人员所需的通用技能。为了获得硕士学位，通常要求你在学士学位的基础上再学习两年，可以使你有资格在高中或社区学院担任心理学讲师，或成为某些行业（如咨询行业）的应用心理学家。硕士水平的心理学家在公共服务机构和私人诊所中很常见（尽管美国的许多州不允许他们自称为“心理学家”）。
p109.en: However, in order to become a full-fledged psychologist, in addition to a bachelor's degree, a great deal of training is required. At the graduate school, students in the psychology department need to study advanced courses in one or more specialized fields, while developing the common skills required by scholars and researchers. In order to obtain a master's degree, you are usually required to study for another two years on the basis of a bachelor's degree, which would qualify you to serve as a psychologist at a high school or community college, or as an applied psychologist in certain professions, such as consulting. Master-level psychologists are common in public service institutions and private clinics (although many states in the United States do not allow them to call themselves “psychologists”).

p110.original: 拥有博士学位（如哲学博士学位、心理学博士或教育学博士）的人有最广泛的职业选择（Smith，2002b）。在美国大多数州，心理学从业执照要求博士学位和督导实践经历。博士学位也能为你提供很多职业的从业资格，如在社区学院和大学执教，从事研究以及成为司法心理学专家等。你甚至可以做一名电子游戏研究人员，让电子游戏变得更人性化、更有趣！
p110.en: Persons with a doctorate degree (e.g. a doctorate in philosophy, a doctorate in psychology or a doctorate in education) have the widest choice of occupation (Smith, 2002b). In most states of the United States, the licensing of psychology requires a doctorate and supervision of practical experience. Doctorate degrees can also provide you with professional qualifications in a number of professions, such as teaching at community colleges and universities, conducting research and becoming a specialist in judicial psychology. You can even be a video game researcher and make video games more human and interesting!
